identity.core_loop: Follow the wind to a goal, fight or sneak through a camp, duel, write a haiku, ride on.
identity.ui_and_game_feel: Weighty and cinematic; swordplay is about stance and timing.

hud_coverage.method: Oracle study from public knowledge of the game, in our own words; not yet measured on capture

information_grammar.note: The guiding wind replaces the waypoint: grass, leaves and Jin's hair point the way. Birds and foxes lead to secrets; the HUD fades almost completely.

identity.art_direction: Cinematic realism pushed toward painted colour: fields of red and gold, wind in everything.

rendering.source: derived from the art note by rendering_notes.RULES

tricks: Performance capture of the cast carries each character's personality; casting changed characters to fit performers
Sword stances change the whole idle and attack set, so a stance swap reads instantly
Wind drives hair, cloth, grass and leaves together, so even a still character looks alive
motion.lesson: Capture the performer, then let one wind signal move cloth and hair so idle never looks frozen.

identity.lessons_for_abbies_world: Navigation by wind is the best diegetic waypoint we know. Let wind, animals and light lead the player in Abbie's World.
